fine_lines.title: clutch at straws vs throw your toys out of the pram
words: throw your toys out of the pram
fine_lines.explanation_ar: clutch at straws = تحاول حلولاً يائسة وضعيفة لأن الموقف صعب. throw your toys out of the pram = تتصرف كالطفل وتغضب بشكل مبالغ فيه لأنك لم تحصل على ما تريد.
fine_lines.explanation_en: 'Clutch at straws' = try desperate ideas that probably won't work. 'Throw your toys out of the pram' = act like a child and get very angry when you don't get what you want.

examples.sentence: Blaming the weather for my bad essay was clutching at straws.

examples.word: throw your toys out of the pram
examples.sentence: He threw his toys out of the pram when they gave the job to someone else.

fine_lines.title: slow walk vs walk slowly
fine_lines.explanation_ar: walk slowly معناها الحرفي: يمشي ببطء. slow-walk something (فعل مركّب) = يؤخّر شيئاً عن قصد ويمنع تقدّمه.
fine_lines.explanation_en: 'Walk slowly' is literal: move on foot at low speed. 'Slow-walk something' means to delay it on purpose and stop it from moving forward.

examples.sentence: Grandma walks slowly with her stick.
The committee is slow-walking our request.

fine_lines.title: touch grass vs rinse and repeat
fine_lines.explanation_ar: touch grass = نصيحة لشخص يقضي وقتاً طويلاً على الإنترنت: اخرج وعُد إلى العالم الحقيقي. rinse and repeat = تكرار نفس الأفعال الروتينية مرة بعد مرة.
fine_lines.explanation_en: 'Touch grass' is advice to someone who spends too much time online: go outside and reconnect with real life. 'Rinse and repeat' describes doing the same routine again and again.

examples.sentence: You've been gaming for ten hours – go touch grass!
Wake up, work, sleep. Rinse and repeat.

expressions.meaning_en: to delay something on purpose or stop it from progressing
expressions.example: They are slow-walking the new rules so nothing changes.

grammar.title: Verb + adjective/adverb in slang: 'hits different'
grammar.explanation_ar: في القواعد الرسمية نستخدم الظرف بعد الفعل: it hits differently. لكن في العامية الحديثة يقولون it hits different (بدون ly) وهذه عبارة ثابتة. ومثلها: Drive safe! (بدل safely). في الكتابة الرسمية استخدم الظرف.
grammar.explanation_en: In standard grammar an adverb follows a verb: it hits differently. In modern slang people say 'it hits different' as a fixed phrase. Similar: 'Drive safe!' (instead of safely). In formal writing, use the adverb.
examples: Formal: The two plans affect us differently.
Informal: Drive safe! / Formal: Drive safely.
